Stop here for SDE-1. The dual-write problem, why 2PC blocks, and sagas with compensations are the must-know part. The outbox, CDC, event sourcing, CQRS and exactly-once machinery below are SDE-2 depth; at minimum, know the outbox in one sentence and the idempotent consumer stepper.

sections.title: CQRS: separate the write model from the read models
Interview questions
sections.before:
Level 5 - Interview-ready

You might confuse this with... 2PC vs saga: two-phase commit makes several databases commit atomically by holding locks until a coordinator says "commit", so it is consistent but blocks when the coordinator dies; a saga commits each step locally at once and undoes earlier steps with compensations, so it never blocks but other requests can see half-finished state. Outbox vs CDC: the outbox is what you write (an event row in the same transaction as the business change); CDC is how it can be shipped (by tailing the database log). You can use an outbox with a polling relay, CDC without an outbox (raw table changes), or both together.
